derivation: Divide the model by V_ref: V/V_ref = (I/I_ref)^(1/α). Raise both sides to the power α to obtain (V/V_ref)^α = I/I_ref, then multiply by I_ref. Thus I = 2.00 mA × (125/100)^10 = 2.00 mA × 1.25^10.
verification: The current ratio is I/I_ref = 9.31323. Raising it to the power 1/α = 0.1 gives approximately 1.25, so the model returns V ≈ 125 V.
input_problem: A varistor follows V = V_ref (I/I_ref)^(1/α) with V_ref = 100 V, I_ref = 2.00 mA, and α = 10. Find the current I when the voltage is V = 125 V. Assume the model applies for positive voltage and current.
